source.title: From Tempered to Benign Overfitting in ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: Guy Kornowski; Gilad Yehudai; Ohad Shamir

record.tranche_reason: The study tests interpolation and generalization under controlled label noise in shallow ReLU networks, using theoretical analysis and experiments across dimensions. It does not reproduce the original deep-network experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports empirical curves and explicitly states that every experiment correctly classified all noisy training data. It does not test shuffled pixels, Gaussian-noise inputs, explicit regularization, or learning real patterns before noise.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures SGD fitting of independently randomized binary labels and generalization across noise levels in a new synthetic setting. Its empirical interpolation results test V1; its dimension-dependent test-error profiles bear on V4. Most theoretical results assume interpolation rather than establish that training achieves it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's summary is broadly correct but should retain the theoretical assumptions: conditional on interpolation and specified margin-solution assumptions, low-dimensional two-layer ReLU networks exhibit tempered overfitting and high-dimensional networks can exhibit benign overfitting. Experiments suggest a gradual transition with dimension, little sensitivity to tested widths, and similar behavior at depth three. Bias-less architectures can instead exhibit catastrophic overfitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes 2-layer ReLU networks and empirically trains fully connected 2- or 3-layer networks on synthetic spherical inputs with controlled label noise; it does not reproduce the original image experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The clean test-error profile changes with input dimension relative to sample size; width has little apparent effect in the tested 2-layer settings, and the tested 3-layer curve looks similar to the 2-layer curve.
record.problems: Empirical clean-test-error curves are presented in figures without numeric values in the text; only 10 random seeds are used. The settings are synthetic low- or high-dimensional spherical inputs, not image datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No separate numeric figure-value rows are possible from the supplied text; figures show curves over dimensions and noise levels without textually stated point values. Reported aggregate training interpolation and text-described trends are retained.

untested.parts: No true-label p=0 experiment establishes unchanged hyperparameters relative to clean training. The reported test measure uses clean constant-positive labels; test error against fresh independent random labels at p=0.5 is necessarily chance but is not empirically reported.
No convergence-time comparison between true and random labels or across corruption fractions. A common 20000-epoch budget and unchanged results at 100000 epochs do not measure fitting speed.
No experiments fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs. A theoretical distribution-extension remark does not demonstrate SGD fitting those inputs.

No empirical p=0 baseline, exact clean-test-error trajectories or verified chance endpoint. The constant-positive target does not test learning nonconstant real-data structure. Binary flipping at p=0.5 produces fully random labels; it is not 100% label inversion.
No controlled comparisons of weight decay, dropout or augmentation, or their removal on true-label generalization.
No training trajectories separating acquisition of shared patterns from memorization of noisy labels.

missing.what: Conditional one-dimensional generalization bounds: Theorem 3.1 gives polynomial bounds in p for KKT points; Theorem 3.2 gives Θ(p) expected clean test error for local minima. Interpolation is assumed.

Conditional high-dimensional benign-overfitting guarantees: clean test error at most epsilon under the stated dimension, sample-size, noise and norm assumptions, or fixed-output-weight and width assumptions. These do not prove SGD reaches interpolation.

Architecture-dependent failures: bias-less width-two interpolants with a negative example have clean test error at least 1/2; Proposition 4.6 constructs interpolating KKT points with error at least 1/2 minus 2^(-|I_minus|) for orthogonal inputs.

record.verdict_notes: The original V4 limits_scope reason is invalid: positive clean test error near p=0.5 agrees with degradation. The relevant qualification is near-zero clean error at positive lower noise in high dimensions. For this distribution, noisy-label test error equals p + (1−2p) times clean test error; at p=0.5 it is exactly 1/2 regardless of the reported clean error. Row states marked partial reflect combined measures and mixed conditions; zero training error itself is observed in every empirical row.

versions.untested_parts: The experiment includes noise level p=0.5, but does not explicitly report that test error is at chance there, or compare against the same network trained on true labels.
The empirical sweep reports clean test error, but the text does not establish that test error rises steadily to chance as p approaches 0.5.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully connected neural network
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD and logistic (cross-entropy) loss on noisy labels; authors state all experiments correctly classified every training example.
rows.measure: Training classification error; clean test error as a function of label-noise level.
rows.value: All experiments correctly classified all of the (inherently noisy) training data; clean test error plotted in Figure 1.
rows.uncertainty: 10 random-seed runs; plots averaged over runs.
rows.note: The text gives the perfect training classification result for all experiments in aggregate, and describes Figure 1 as showing a gradual transition from tempered to benign behavior as dimension increases. Figure values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: Zero training error is observed throughout, including fully random labels at p=0.5. The combined row needs separate training-error and clean-test-error results by dimension: V4's degradation appears in tempered regimes but weakens in benign regimes. Dimensions are 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000. Training uses learning rate 0.1 for 20000 epochs.
